correctness.rationale: The cardinal coefficients sum to 1 and on each half-interval at most one is negative, by at most 1/8. On the upper half, a single-axis interpolation of a monotone row can be written as its minimum plus two nonnegative increments, and lies in [0,9/8]; interpolating those values along the other axis bounds the result below by −9/64. When both half-intervals are lower, write the negative coefficients as −a and −b. The positive-positive interior may be discarded for a lower bound. Each entry multiplying a negative tensor weight is at most f₂₂; retaining the positive corner gives the bound −[a(1+b)+b(1+a)−ab]f₂₂≥−17/64. This covers the continuum and the boundaries. The data that are 1 on the top-index row or column and 0 elsewhere give equality at (1/4,1/4). Reflection in both coordinates and complement transfer the lower extremum to the upper one. Mixing either witness with (i+j)/4 gives strict data without changing the end range, and converges to the witnesses. Thus strict sharpness is limiting only. Affine normalization preserves both sharp constants.

value.rationale: The standard uniform biquadratic reconstruction is a natural object for checking whether monotone grid data stay within range. The gain over the unrestricted envelope is numerically modest, but the sharp bound quantifies the required buffer (more than a quarter of the data range on each side), provides an explicit monotone witness and rules out fixing the defect by requiring strict nodal monotonicity alone. The exact coupled-data restriction and witness are useful where a shape- or range-preserving reconstruction is needed.
